text:
ben: thanks for today's all-hands — quick follow-ups on runtime roadmap items. three short Qs: kernel switching policy under load, preferred batching thresholds for interactive vs bulk, and KV cache invalidation during rollouts. anyone from runtime/infra see this?
lin: good Qs. short answers first: 1) kernel switch is conservative — we avoid swapping mid-request unless latency breach is sustained, 2) interactive vs bulk batching defaults differ, 3) cache invalidation is rollout-triggered + TTL. happy to expand.
ben: can you expand on "conservative"? curious about edge cases where 95th pct latency spikes for a small subset of models.
lin: sure — we look at a 60s window and require sustained 95th > target and increased queue depth before switching kernels. we also factor in in-flight token cost to avoid oscillation.
maya: adding operations note: we prefer switching at steady-state rather than transient spikes. ops-bot will flag candidate switches for manual review when it's a cross-tenant change.
alex: for batching thresholds: interactive defaults to max_batch_size=16 and soft_latency=50ms; bulk jobs use max_batch_size=256 and soft_latency=200ms. those are current platform defaults but can be tuned per route.
sara: are those numbers public in the console as suggestions? it'd be great if Optimize could recommend them per workload.
maya: yes — Optimize will surface suggested max_batch_size and latency targets based on recent traffic patterns. plan is to show a delta estimate: cost/token delta + expected p95 impact.
ben: about cache invalidation — is it purely TTL-based or do we have a model-rollout hook to drop affected prefixes?
lin: rollout hook exists. when you pin a new model version we can do targeted KV prefix invalidation for the affected model id. default TTL is 30m for prefixes but the rollout action triggers immediate invalidation when enabled.
ben: how do we avoid cache stampedes after invalidation?
lin: two strategies: staggered invalidation (canary-first) and randomized early-refresh by downstream clients. plus an optional grace window where stale entries served for N requests while backend warms.
alex: also note: cache is sharded by tenant+model+prefix-hash so invalidation scope is narrow.
sara: any change to latency SLOs when kernel switches happen?
maya: we try to keep SLOs stable. the routing policy prefers lower-latency kernels for high-tier customers. on switch we run a canary for a slice, monitor p50/p95 for 5 minutes, then roll. immediate rollbacks are automatic if p95 increases > configured delta.
ben: wow thanks — last ask: where can I find the rollout + kernel policy docs?
lin: docs in Console → Runtime → Routing → "Kernel & Rollout Policies" and a short runbook at /internal/runbooks/kernel-switch.md (ops-only).
ben: perfect. i'll follow up with a short doc request for product so recommendations are clearer for PMs. thanks everyone :rocket:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout for model redwood-alpha on 1868130600 by maya.
ops-bot: alert: automated kernel switch suggested for model-test-42 based on 5m sustained p95 breach. reviewer: @lin
lin: acknowledged, will look at logs and mute if false positive.
maya: ping me if you need manual hold — i'm on standby this afternoon.
ben: great — closing this thread, feel free to reply if more Qs.
